findings.reason: a worker dispatched at `_apply_move` finds a pure index-only applier and cannot write a second document from it; the plan must name the write layer that owns both writes (the caller in mcp_edit_plan.py, or the op carrying the plan path), or the node builds a mechanism that cannot run.
findings.text: §8 says "`_apply_move` in `reckon/_store.py` writes the moved plan's `plan-sprint` through the plan's own store write in the same call as the two sprint resources", but `_apply_move` (reckon/_store.py:3404) refuses anything but the index (`if not is_index: raise OpError("move op is index-only")`, :3405-3406), it receives only `(working, op, is_index, warnings)` and no repository, path or store handle, and the layer that dispatches it is documented "Pure: never touches disk or version fields" (`apply_ops`, reckon/_store.py:3927). Its only production caller (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1452) applies one batch to one document, and the plan document is a different document from the index. So the write §8 describes cannot be reached from the site §8 names, and no caller is named for it

findings.reason: without declared write paths the node cannot be fenced to `reckon/_store.py` and its test, and the coordinator has no path to audit the landing against.
findings.text: §8 ends without the `Write paths:` line every other section carries, and names no evidence or gate log path, so nothing in the node sits on a durable path a later reader can open

findings.reason: §1–§7 each name their test file so the gate is one runnable command; §8's gate cannot be dispatched or re-run by id.
findings.text: the measure reads "a test moves a plan between two sprints", naming no test file, so the gate is not a command anyone can run and §4's audit clause ("§4's audit reports no mismatch after a move") names no invocation either

findings.reason: dispatched in the order the plan now allows (§6 first), §6 writes exactly the stale `plan-sprint` state §8 is written to prevent, so the ordering the plan leaves unstated decides whether §8's fix is exercised before or after the moves it protects.
findings.text: §8 declares no `depends-on` and no "runs after" line, while §6 (line 144, `implementable`, all three gates `passed`) is open and its deliverable is to "move every live S22 member into an advancing sprint or the backlog", which is the sprint move §8 exists to fix; §6's own §4 audit would report the mismatches §8 removes

rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §8 declares no write paths and no evidence or log path, alone among §1–§7.
